phases.name: Anchor LinkedIn extraction on the job link, not block position, to stop silent title/company/location shift

steps.name: Regression test pinning the header-shift defect (RED)
criteria: A block containing two job cards yields two rows, not one — the trailing card is no longer dropped.
Fixture 1a05bf0e7d2000d8 (preamble) yields the true title/company/location triple, not the preamble text, for its job.
Fixture 1a05c5fb49972c37 (raw HTML + Manage alerts + other-alerts header) yields correct triples for both its primary and cross-sell cards.
Fixture 1a09be37fadab08b (alert-created confirmation) yields the real title/company/location, not the confirmation sentences.
Fixture 1a067f6097dc5f98 (Edit alert + token lines) yields the correct triple with location no longer lost.
steps.scenario_name: a block with an unfiltered preamble line no longer shifts the extracted title/company/location triple
steps.implementation_notes: Fixtures MUST be copied byte-for-byte from real cached messages (.cache/messages/2026-09/*.json, gitignored) — never hand-written; this project already had one incident (DR-0007) caused by an invented test model. Commit copies to fixtures/linkedin/, redacting any toRecipients field to me@example.invalid the way fixtures/spill/ already does. Named real examples to copy: 1a05bf0e7d2000d8 (preamble), 1a05c5fb49972c37 (raw HTML + Manage alerts: + other-alerts header), 1a09be37fadab08b (alert-created confirmation, two preamble lines), 1a067f6097dc5f98 (Edit alert + token lines). This test MUST fail against the current shipped parser — confirm RED before handing off to 01-02. Root cause: docs/feature/fix-linkedin-header-shift/rca.md (positional "first three non-noise lines" rule, no structural anchor). TEST PARADIGM: this is a regression/golden-fixture test against real captured messages, not a property — EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: fixture-anchored extraction defect, not a quantifiable invariant over generated input. Compensate with the existing property-style boundary coverage already in coverage.test.mjs at the adjacent core-module level. PATH CORRECTION (orchestrator, 2026-09-14): regression fixtures go to fixtures/linkedin-variants/, NOT fixtures/linkedin/. The walking-skeleton acceptance test scans fixtures/linkedin/ directory-wide via json-message-reader readAll() and asserts row counts against it, so adding files there drops it to 7/8. Keeping the corpora separate preserves that test without weakening any assertion.

steps.name: Anchor-on-link extraction fix (GREEN)
criteria: Extraction anchors on each `/jobs/view/{id}` occurrence per block, walking backward past trailing noise to take the last three lines as title/company/location.
Every job link in a multi-card block produces its own row; no card is silently dropped.
All five existing fixtures/linkedin fixtures still produce their previously-passing title/company/location values unchanged.
Subject-line salary attaches only to the first extracted job of a message; canonical `/jobs/view/{id}/` link reconstruction is preserved.
tests/regression/job-alert-harvester/linkedin-block-anchor.test.mjs and the existing 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both pass.
steps.scenario_name: a block with an unfiltered preamble line no longer shifts the extracted title/company/location triple
steps.implementation_notes: Approved direction (user decision 2026-09-14, rca.md § Proposed Fix): locate every `View job:` line per block, walk backward past the closed trailing-noise set (This company is actively hiring / Apply with resume & profile / N connection(s) / N company alumni / N school alumni / Promoted / Easy Apply / Actively recruiting / blank lines), take the next three lines as [location, company, title] reversed. linkedin:{jobId} dedup keys come from the URL match, independent of the triple, so a full re-parse of the cache repairs history without changing keys — the repair path DR-0001 (persist what cannot be re-derived) exists for exactly this. Hard constraints: Node 22, ESM, Vitest; dependencies are xlsx and vitest only, no new dependency; src/core/ stays pure — no classes, no mutation, no node: imports. Do not widen NOISE_LINE preamble entries; anchoring makes them unnecessary (removing is optional cleanup, not required here).

steps.name: Close the trailing-noise set over singular alum counts (RED+GREEN)
criteria: A job card whose trailing noise reads '1 company alum' or '1 school alum' (singular) extracts the same title/company/location triple as the plural 'N company alumni' form.
The existing plural forms keep matching; no other noise pattern changes.
The full LinkedIn cache corpus yields zero Jobs rows whose Company is a location string and zero whose Location is an alum count.
tests/regression/job-alert-harvester/linkedin-block-anchor.test.mjs and the 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both stay green.
steps.scenario_name: a singular alum count is trailing noise, not a meaningful line
steps.implementation_notes: Discovered post-01-02 against the live 59-message cache, not from the original brief. LinkedIn emits '1 company alum' and '1 school alum' in the singular; TRAILING_NOISE_LINE only matches /^\d+ company alumni$/ and /^\d+ school alumni$/, so the singular line counts as meaningful and tripleAbove() shifts the whole triple by one — title takes the company, company takes the location, location takes the alum count. Corpus evidence: 8 occurrences of '1 company alum' and 3 of '1 school alum'; 7 distinct rows wrong, e.g. job 4445955126 yields [Worldpay, 'London Area, United Kingdom', '1 company alum'] where the raw mail reads 'Release Train Engineer' / 'Worldpay' / 'London Area, United Kingdom'. This is the same defect class as 01-02 (an incomplete closed set), not a regression from it. Fix is to make the plural optional in both patterns; do not broaden them beyond alum/alumni.

steps.name: Treat a per-card salary line as trailing noise (RED+GREEN)
criteria: A job card carrying a salary line below its location (e.g. '£59K-£78K / year') extracts the same title/company/location triple as a card without one.
The subject-line salary behaviour is unchanged: parseSalaryFromSubject still attaches the subject salary to the headline job only.
The full cache corpus yields zero Jobs rows whose Location starts with '£'.
The regression test and the 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both stay green.
steps.scenario_name: a per-card salary line is trailing noise, not the location
steps.implementation_notes: Third instance of the same defect class as 01-02 and 01-03: the trailing-noise set is a denylist and this line was not in it. Corpus evidence: 3 of 198 job cards carry a salary line immediately below the location, e.g. job 4456258182 raw reads 'Senior Scrum Master' / 'Leonardo' / 'Gloucester' / '£59K-£78K / year', and tripleAbove() takes the last three as [£59K-£78K / year, Gloucester, Leonardo], yielding title=Leonardo, company=Gloucester, location=£59K-£78K / year. Add a salary-shaped pattern to TRAILING_NOISE_LINE anchored on a leading £ (optionally preceded by 'up to'); keep it tight enough that it cannot match a company or location. DISCARDING the value is deliberate for this step: capturing per-card salary into Min/Max Salary (annual) is an emerged requirement awaiting a decision, not part of this fix.

steps.name: Capture the per-card salary instead of discarding it (RED+GREEN)
criteria: A job card carrying '£65K-£74K / year' yields minSalary 65000 and maxSalary 74000 on that job's row.
A card-level salary takes precedence over the subject-line salary for the same job, because the card carries a range where the subject carries only a ceiling.
The subject-line salary still attaches to the headline job only, and still applies where the card carries no salary of its own.
A card salary denominated per hour or per day is recognised so it cannot shift the title/company/location triple, but is written to no salary column.
The triple extraction from 01-04 is unchanged: no row's title, company or location changes value.
The regression test and the 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both stay green.
steps.scenario_name: a per-card salary range populates both min and max, beating the subject ceiling
steps.implementation_notes: EMERGED REQUIREMENT approved by the user 2026-09-14 — not a defect. Reverses the deliberate discard in 01-04: 'Salary is an important element, rarely specified in ads, not noise.' Corpus evidence: Min Salary (annual) is empty for all 146 rows because all 13 subject-line salaries are 'up to £X' (ceiling only, min null by design). The 3 per-card lines (£65K-£74K, £45K-£55K, £59K-£78K / year) are the corpus's only salary RANGES, so they are the sole path to a populated Min. Biffa job 4456258182 shows the precedence case directly: subject 'up to £74K/year' vs card '£65K-£74K / year'. Reuse the existing toAnnualAmount helper rather than writing new magnitude parsing. Note the latent 4th denylist gap: the 01-04 pattern matches only '/ year', so a '/ hour' or '/ day' card line would still shift the triple — close that here. Where those columns land is an open user decision (DR-0004 one-owner-per-column makes Min Salary (hourly) and Day Rate human-owned), so recognise the unit but write no value.

steps.name: Never file an hourly or day rate as an annual salary (RED+GREEN)
criteria: A subject reading 'up to £45/hour' yields no annual salary — Min and Max Salary (annual) are both null for that job.
A subject reading 'up to £500/day' likewise yields no annual salary.
Annual subjects ('up to £74K/year', '£55K-£70K / year') are unaffected and keep their current parsed values.
The parsed rate and its unit remain available on the returned value so a later step can route them to a column without re-parsing.
The regression test and the 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both stay green.
steps.scenario_name: an hourly rate in the subject never becomes an annual salary
steps.implementation_notes: Defect found in the rebuilt workbook 2026-09-14. parseSalaryFromSubject matches 'Financial Accountant at Venture Recruitment Partners: up to £45/hour' and returns {min: null, max: 45}, which core/harvest.mjs writes into 'Max Salary (annual)'. The sheet then reads as a £45-per-year job: syntactically valid, semantically wrong, and invisible to any schema check — the same plausible-but-wrong class DR-0003 was written about. The regex already captures the amount but ignores the unit that follows it. Capture the unit and return annual figures ONLY for per-year amounts. WHERE hourly and day rates should be written is an OPEN USER DECISION and is explicitly NOT part of this step: DR-0004 (one owner per column) makes 'Min Salary (hourly)' and 'Day Rate' human-owned and requires a new '(derived)' sibling column rather than taking the human's. Add no column and write no rate value in this step — only stop the misfiling, and surface the unit so the follow-up is a routing change rather than a reparse.

steps.name: Route hourly and day rates to derived sibling columns (RED+GREEN)
criteria: The Jobs tab gains 'Min Rate (derived)', 'Max Rate (derived)' and 'Rate Unit (derived)', populated from job.rate.
A subject reading 'up to £45/hour' populates Max Rate 45 and Rate Unit 'hour', leaving Min Rate and both annual columns null — a ceiling is never written as a minimum.
A day-denominated rate populates the same three columns with Rate Unit 'day'.
The human-owned 'Min Salary (hourly)' and 'Day Rate' columns are still created blank and never written — DR-0004 one owner per column.
No annual equivalent is computed from a day or hourly rate; the columns stay independent.
All three new columns are registered as harvester-owned in merge.mjs HARVESTER_COLUMNS so a future merge overwrites them with freshly derived values.
The regression test and the 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both stay green.
steps.scenario_name: an hourly rate reaches its derived column without touching the human's
steps.implementation_notes: User decision 2026-09-14 approving the DR-0004-conformant option: a parser that learns to derive a human-owned value gets a '(derived)' sibling rather than taking the human's column. The user also declined an annual-equivalent conversion from day rates — the assumption (working days per year, IR35 status) would be invented by the parser and invisible in the sheet. DEVIATION from the column names put to the user, flagged to them in the same turn: the approved pair was 'Min Salary (hourly) (derived)' and 'Day Rate (derived)'. Every rate in the corpus is 'up to £X' — a CEILING — so writing it to a column named Min would repeat the exact misfiling 01-06 just fixed, and a per-unit pair would need four columns, which DR-0004's own exception clause warns against ('sibling columns proliferate'). One unit-tagged triple covers hour and day, extends to any future unit, and mirrors the annual Min/Max pair. Consumes the rate surface 01-06 added ({min, max, unit} on job.rate), so this is routing, not reparsing. Three files: JOBS_COLUMNS and toJobsRow in src/core/harvest.mjs, HARVESTER_COLUMNS in src/core/merge.mjs. Place the three columns immediately after 'Day Rate' in JOBS_COLUMNS; note that DR-0004 rule 3 separately requires the MERGE path to append new columns to the right of an existing sheet's header, a different code path (planMerge, still a RED scaffold).

steps.name: The derived rate columns carry only non-annual rates (RED+GREEN)
criteria: A job whose rate unit is 'year' leaves Min Rate (derived), Max Rate (derived) and Rate Unit (derived) all null — its figures belong in the annual columns only.
A job whose rate unit is 'hour' or 'day' still populates all three derived columns as in 01-07.
No job ever carries a value in both the annual pair and the derived rate columns.
The annual columns are unchanged: 10 rows carry an annual salary and 3 carry a full range.
The regression test and the 8/8 walking-skeleton acceptance test both stay green.
steps.scenario_name: an annual salary never appears in the derived rate columns
steps.implementation_notes: Defect introduced by 01-07 and caught in the rebuilt workbook 2026-09-14. toJobsRow routes job.rate into the derived columns unconditionally, so 7 of the 8 rate-bearing rows carry Rate Unit 'year' and restate their annual figures. Worse, the two pairs DISAGREE where the sources differ: the Biffa row (linkedin job in fixtures, IT Product Delivery Manager) shows annual 65000-74000 from its card range but Min Rate blank / Max Rate 74000 from the subject ceiling — the same job described two ways in one row, which is the plausible-but-wrong class DR-0003 was written about. The derived rate columns exist for rates the annual columns cannot express; gate them on unit !== 'year'. Routing change only in src/core/harvest.mjs toJobsRow — do not touch the parser, and leave job.rate itself carrying the year unit, which is correct at the parser boundary.
